LESSON: IMITATION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING AND
Topic 1.1: Imitation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Imitation. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family
   In simple words: practise until you can respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Imitation using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Imitation in the examples.
2. Explain Imitation to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Imitation.
4. Show that you can: respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Imitation using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Imitation important for a Grade 3 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Learners role play conversations in different appropriately setups (church, market, home etc) c) respond appropriately to
2. Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family d) appreciate the importance
3. Has difficulty in choosing language with different people different people assistance appropriate words appropriate words when
4. Listens and provides appropriate during conversation conversing with different people

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. respond appropriately to  Learners take turns as they participate in panel conversations with varied discussions on issues related to self, home, and audiences family

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
